log.text:
The last light lies copper-red across Oakhollow’s cobbles, catching on the stone well and the iron latch of the grain storehouse. Villagers argue in tight knots: some point toward the road and mutter about goblins, others glance at the forge, the inn, and one another. Seed grain has vanished before planting, and without it several families may lose the harvest.

You were called here because the village wants outsiders—or someone convenient—to blame, while the truth is still close enough to touch. Orrin Vale stands by the locked storehouse, smoothing the same fold in his sleeve; Tessa Reed brushes dirt from her cuffs near the well, Mara Venn taps a spoon against her palm outside the inn, and Hobb Fen watches from the forge through a veil of coal smoke.

The first useful questions are waiting in plain sight: the lock, the rumors, and whatever tracks someone was eager for you to notice. What do you do?

pc:pc-1-fighter.name: Aldric

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Versatile (1d10) two-handed — forgoing the shield drops AC to 17.

features.name: Fighting Style: Defense
features.text: +1 AC while wearing armor (already in AC 19).

features.name: Second Wind
features.text: Bonus action, 1/short rest: regain 1d10+1 hit points.

pc:pc-1-fighter.backstory: Aldric once guarded seed and livestock caravans along the King’s Road. After refusing to let a wealthy trader bully a starving hamlet, he left caravan work with a worn badge and a distrust of justice that protects only the powerful.

pc:pc-2-wizard.name: Elara

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.text: Once/day on a short rest, recover spell slots totaling up to half your wizard level (rounded up).

pc:pc-2-wizard.backstory: Elara learned practical magic from solitary village tutors, using small spells to preserve food, mend tools, and read weather signs. She wants to prove that careful reasoning matters as much as grand arcane displays.

pc:pc-3-rogue.name: Pip

features.name: Sneak Attack (1d6)
features.text: Once per turn, +1d6 damage on a hit with advantage, or when an ally is adjacent to the target.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Double proficiency on Stealth and Investigation.

pc:pc-3-rogue.backstory: Pip grew up carrying messages and small parcels between roadside villages, learning every unofficial mark used by carters, gamblers, and smugglers. Pip now seeks honest work without losing the instincts that kept them safe.

adventure.pitch: A grounded village mystery about trust, debt, and the danger of blaming outsiders too quickly. The party must uncover who is stealing Oakhollow’s seed grain while someone stages crude signs of goblin or wolf involvement.

scene:b1.title: The Green at Dusk
scene:b1.summary: The party hears competing accounts of the theft and can question witnesses, inspect the storehouse lock, search the green, or follow rumors into the inn and forge. Orrin wants a quiet solution; Tessa insists the tracks point toward the road; Mara knows who was drinking late; Hobb noticed unusual metalwork. Suggested checks: Investigation or Perception to spot the planted clues, Insight to weigh testimony, and Persuasion to calm the crowd. The blue thread, bent horseshoe, and crow-mark are the first useful leads.

scenePlan.look: A dry cobbled village green surrounds a circular stone well. The Gilded Boar inn, a blacksmith’s forge with coal yard, a small roadside shrine, fenced cottages, and the locked grain storehouse border the square.
scenePlan.mood: Dusk under a clear, fading sky

scene:b2.title: The Storehouse Clues
scene:b2.summary: Inside the storehouse, the party can examine the damaged latch, question the watch volunteer, search spilled chaff, or visit the forge to compare the bent horseshoe. A few giant rats have been attracted by the grain and may cause a brief complication, but they are not responsible for the theft. The evidence shows the door was opened with a copied key, sacks were dragged toward the rear lane, and a smear of blue wool came from Jory’s work cloak. Suggested checks: Investigation, Survival, or thieves’ tools to reconstruct the entry; Medicine or Nature to distinguish animal damage from deliberate staging.

scenePlan.look: A low timber storehouse stands inside a fenced yard, with stacked grain bins, a barred front door, a narrow rear lane, and a broken section of plank fence opening toward fields.
scenePlan.mood: Dim lantern light with stale, dusty air

scene:b3.title: The Hedgerow Trail
scene:b3.summary: The rear trail crosses kitchen gardens, a drainage ditch, and a thorn hedgerow before reaching the King’s Road. The party can track the dragged sacks, question field workers, search for the source of the blue wool, or use Pip’s road sense to identify the crow-mark as a signal rather than a monster sign. A frightened wolf may be driven away, avoided, or calmed; its presence explains some tracks but not the theft. The trail reveals a handcart route toward the abandoned toll shed, while a dropped betting token links Jory to a debt. Suggested checks: Survival, Animal Handling, or Sleight of Hand.

scenePlan.look: Narrow crop fields and vegetable plots divide the land into rectangles, with a muddy drainage ditch, thorn hedgerow, footbridge, and cart track leading toward the King’s Road.
scenePlan.mood: Cool evening with long shadows and rising mist

scene:b4.title: The Abandoned Toll Shed
scene:b4.summary: The party reaches the derelict toll shed and finds Jory with two bandits guarding the stolen grain. They may sneak in, bargain over repayment, expose the bandits’ weak position, or confront them openly. Jory is frightened rather than cruel and can be separated from the bandits if offered a path to restitution. The bandits possess the copied storehouse key and confirm that the crow-mark was their meeting signal. Suggested checks: Stealth, Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion; combat is possible if talks fail.

scenePlan.look: A sagging timber toll shed sits beside the King’s Road, surrounded by nettles and a shallow ditch. Grain sacks fill the shed’s rear, while a handcart, hitching post, collapsed lean-to, and broken toll gate occupy the roadside.
scenePlan.mood: Moonlit night with cold wind through broken boards

scene:b5.title: Truth on the Green
scene:b5.summary: The party returns to Oakhollow with the grain and the truth. Orrin can hold a public accounting, Mara can pressure Jory to speak plainly, or the party can privately negotiate restitution before the gathering. The village must decide whether Jory works off the debt and whether the bandits’ coercion is reported to road authorities. Aldric’s experience with caravan justice helps frame a fair punishment; Elara can explain the staged signs; Pip can display the copied key and signal mark. The final image is seed grain being carried back into the storehouse as the well bell rings.

scenePlan.look: The same cobbled green is now lit by lanterns, with villagers gathered around the stone well. The inn, forge, shrine, storehouse, and road entrance form a clear ring around the meeting place.
scenePlan.mood: Quiet late night beneath bright stars

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.text: Advantage on an attack if an ally is within 5 ft. of the target.

blueprint.premise: A grounded village mystery about trust, debt, and the danger of blaming outsiders too quickly. The party must uncover who is stealing Oakhollow’s seed grain while someone stages crude signs of goblin or wolf involvement.
blueprint.centralProblem: Three sacks of seed grain have vanished from Oakhollow’s locked storehouse. The culprit, Jory Pike, has been coerced by passing bandits after gambling away his earnings; he planted misleading tracks and marks to hide the theft, but the remaining grain is still held at an abandoned roadside toll shed.
blueprint.intendedEnding: At the old toll shed, the party confronts Jory and the bandits, recovers the remaining seed grain, and brings the truth back to Oakhollow. Jory confesses, agrees to repay the village through labor, and the reeve publicly clears innocent travelers and villagers of suspicion.
blueprint.opening: At dusk, the party stands together on Oakhollow’s dry cobbled green beside its stone well, with the Gilded Boar inn, blacksmith’s forge, and small roadside shrine around them. Villagers are arguing over the vanished grain while the reeve asks capable strangers to investigate before panic turns into accusations.

spine.intent: Establish the mystery and prevent a scapegoat from being chosen.
Prove the theft was deliberate and human.
Identify the toll shed and connect Jory to the debt.
Confront the perpetrators and secure a confession.
Return the harvest supply and settle the village’s response.

brief.activeBeatIntent: Turn village suspicion into a choice between investigating the locked storehouse and following the staged outsider clues, while keeping trust at stake.

reachable.hook: The reeve offers access to the storehouse, where a careful look may reveal how the theft was staged and who could have entered.
Freshly planted tracks and crude marks lead toward the hedgerow, tempting the party to pursue an apparent goblin or wolf culprit.

clocks: The missing seed must be recovered before planting season worsens the village’s fear and desperation.
Rumors are hardening into blame against outsiders and anyone who cannot account for their movements.
brief.notes: The central route remains open. Early attention to the storehouse can expose the staged evidence; pursuing the hedgerow can still lead onward, but the party may need to question whether the trail is meant to be found.

voice.tic: Keeps smoothing the same fold in his sleeve while speaking formally.
voice.want: To protect Oakhollow’s harvest and reputation.
voice.fear: That panic will turn neighbors against one another.

voice.tic: Taps a wooden spoon against her palm when impatient.
voice.want: To keep the village fed and honest.
voice.fear: That the innocent will be punished while the desperate are ignored.

voice.tic: Answers questions with a grunt, then adds one precise observation.
voice.want: To prove his forgework was not involved in the copied key.
voice.fear: Being blamed for a crime committed with his tools.

voice.tic: Brushes dirt from her sleeves whenever she gets excited.
voice.want: To save her family’s seed allotment.
voice.fear: Having to abandon her farm after one failed planting.

voice.tic: Rubs his thumb over a worn betting token and avoids eye contact.
voice.want: To escape the bandits’ debt and keep his family from learning of it.
voice.fear: That confession will cost him his home and standing.

plant:blue-thread.what: A blue wool thread caught on the storehouse latch identifies Jory’s work cloak later.

plant:bent-horseshoe.what: A distinctive bent horseshoe impression links the handcart to the forge and Jory’s route.

plant:crow-mark.what: A chalk crow on the shrine wall first looks like a threat but later proves to be the bandits’ meeting signal.

plant:aldric-badge.what: A worn caravan badge carried by Aldric earns Mara’s trust and lets him recognize the bandits’ road-debt tactics.
